Dr. Karadzic indicated more than once, it was certainly during the speech that he gave in -- on the 1st of November or the 31st of October, 1991, to SDS officials in connection with the upcoming plebiscite, that although the SDS did have power, have majorities in the Assemblies and so forth of particular -- of many municipalities, they had not exercised that power fully and that they should do so by getting rid of directors of departments and other officials that were not fully obedient to the SDS line. So there is a difference between winning the election and getting a majority and actually getting control of all the levers of power within each municipality, which was a process that Dr. Karadzic wanted to see continue. Now, take-over would refer here to removing those municipalities or regions from the authority of the central government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. For instance, the decision on the formation of the Autonomous Region of Krajina in September 1991 specifically stated that that region was to be a federal unit in Yugoslavia and that the law of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina would only apply in that region insofar as it was not in contradiction to federal law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What are the laws, Dr. Treanor, and constitutions that had priority, the federal ones or the republic ones?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a legal, constitutional question, but I would assume as a layman that the authorities in any particular republic would have to obey the laws and adhere to the constitution of that republic. By the way, the Republic of Serbia in September 1990 had adopted a new constitution. I believe I cited a speech that Mr. Milosevic gave to the Serbian Assembly during the course of that process. Anyway, that new constitution of the Republic of Serbia, that is, a full republic, had a clause that stated basically the same thing, that is, that the laws of Serbia were going to be paramount over any federal laws if there was a conflict of interest between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the decisions of the Constitutional Court in Yugoslavia that quashed similar decisions by Slovenia, Croatia, and even Bosnia-Herzegovina, the laws that were not in keeping with the federal constitution? Don't these decisions prove the priority of federal legislation over republican legislation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think they show that the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia thought that the decisions you're referring to contravened the Constitution of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This would require a debate with you, Dr. Treanor. Although I was opposing the decisions of Bosnian Krajina, did this Bosnian Krajina proclaim its loyalty to federal laws over republican laws that were trying to undermine federal laws? The basic question is: What is wrong with Krajina's demand that federal laws be applied rather than republican laws if the latter run counter to federal legislation? Your interpretation changes the essence. The essence is that federal laws and federal constitution have primacy. Is that your basic conclusion, that it's the other way around?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I was trying to avoid making that type of conclusion because it's a legal and constitutional question. The autonomous region had basically said it itself of its own decision as a federal unit in Yugoslavia, which, as far as I know, would not have been in conformity with either the Bosnian constitution or the Yugoslav constitution. By the way, the previous question as to the constitutional court, I think maybe we can both agree that Slovenia and Croatia rather happily ignored the decisions of the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at paragraph 112 in your document, 529 -- sorry, 592. [In English] "Over the next few months, Assemblies of the Serbian people, in fact, created Serbian municipalities in a number of municipalities in which Serbs were in the majority -- in the minority, though in one or more municipalities there was opposition to the process within the SDS. The Serbian municipalities for which documentation is available claims to be formed from Serbian portions of the existing municipalities or listed the towns and villages of which they were to be composed. The Serbian municipalities initially functioned as parallel entities and operated alongside the existing municipal organs."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 65 ter 606.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You note here that Serbian municipalities are being established from Serbian settlements and Serbian parts of joint, mixed, municipalities. You probably did not get the interpretation of the question. The question was: Is that right? Look at the document, please. Do you see that an agreement was reached in Vlasenica municipality to create a Serbian municipality and a Muslim municipality in Vlasenica, whereas a separate municipality Milici is still a separate municipality today. Do you know that this agreement was made in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware that there were agreements in certain areas, which is one reason why the recommendation for the formation of Serbian municipalities passed by the Bosnian Serb Assembly in November or December 1991 was a recommendation and not an order or a decision because certain deputies said that they were having negotiations in their municipalities which were going well and that that type of move may upset those negotiations. So in certain areas, this apparently being one of them, there were such agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report did you refer to this peaceful -- peaceful -- peace-making way of transforming municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought that the procedure that had been recommended to the -- by the Bosnian Serb Assembly to Serbian council members in the municipalities in which they were in a minority but felt that they were being out-voted, ignored by their colleagues, was a -- basically a peaceful procedure. As for this particular document, I can see that I cite a lot of documents in the report. I don't know whether that one is in there. I believe that the text of this report was not quoted in the report, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the report contain the information that this process provided good results and worked rather well, that the transformation was successful in several places?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to study this document and others in the context of -- to answer that, but it would seem to indicate that in that area there was an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With respect to the issue raised by Mr. Tieger regarding D1285, I looked at the document. There's a slight difference. At the end of the page, P938, there's a signature, while Defence version, I don't see any signature. And moreover, the Prosecution's version is more legible. So I will leave it in your hands whether you are minded to withdraw the Defence version. In the meantime, this will be admitted and we give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1286, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm advised that you have ten minutes to conclude your cross-examination in the time allotted to you. How much would you need to conclude your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I haven't dealt with regionalisation, SDS, JNA, and the paramilitary, and the Chamber made its decision before it became aware of the fact that the interviews made with -- by the Prosecution with Mr. Cizmovic exist. So I would like to ask you to take that into account. It's a new element that gives you a good reason to give me an extension at least until the end of today's session and hopefully at least one session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much would you need for your re-examination, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No more than a half-hour, and I would estimate at this point in time less, Your Honour. But I think I would say that's -- probably 20 to 30 minutes is my estimate. That's sometimes amiss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will have the whole session of today, minus 20 minutes for the re-direct of Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we cannot have an extended day today, can we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's another sitting in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now call --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to paragraph 113 in your document 592. You talk about associations of municipalities and you say it is a level in between -- [In English] "... in the SRBH regional level organisation, intermediate between the municipalities and the republic existed for the -- for some republic governmental functions, police, Territorial Defence, but there was no regional level territorial administrative entity as such. Groups of municipalities could nevertheless form 'communities of municipalities' for certain purposes. A number of such 'communities of municipalities' were in fact formed ..." [Interpretation] And so on. [In English] "The concept of 'communities of municipalities' was defined in 1974 SRBH constitution and was redefined by an amendment of the constitution 1989." [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, then, that this method of forming associations of municipalities was stipulated by the constitution, both the Article 119 of the federal constitution and the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your report you claim that Article 276 of the BH constitution and the amendments to the constitution, such as numbers 42, allowed the association of municipalities into separate socio-political communities. It's in your paragraph 115 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You stated that the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina decided that despite clear provisions concerning urban communities of municipalities specified that this was -- that these were not socio-political communities.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the decision is mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that decision then anti-constitutional? Does the decision wrongly interpret the constitution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a legal and constitutional question that -- maybe that court was best equipped to answer it. I believe that the basis of their decision and objection to these communities of municipalities had to do with the fact that they had given themselves certain defence functions which they were not authorised to have under the constitution and the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And are you aware of Article 119 of the Constitution of the SFRY, where it says that municipalities can co-operate, pooling their resources, setting up joint organs, carry out various functions, and that those organs must have special subjective character, special subjective character?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall that article offhand, but I'll take your word that that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that even a municipality has its defence functions and autonomy and defence in case of war and that it can convey that to the community of municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly aware that the municipalities under the doctrine of All People's Defence had defence functions, as did just about everybody in the former Yugoslavia. I'm not aware that they could transfer any of those functions to the communities of municipalities, which seems to be what the constitutional court is objecting to here. The reference in the paragraph and in the -- that court's decision to socio-political communities, that's a Yugoslav term for meaning a governmental unit. A municipality was a socio-political community. The republic was a socio-political community. But the communities of municipalities were not, that is, as stated in paragraph 113, that they were not an intermediate level of government. They were simply a voluntary co-operative of associations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You make that conclusion on the basis of the decision taken by the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina of the 1st of November, which means 15 days after the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which culminated in -- or rather, on the 14th or 15th of October with the declaration on independence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the date of the decision, the 1st of November, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the constitution on which the community of municipalities were based was the 1974 constitution amended in April 1989; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 1994 [sic] constitution had been amended any number of times, including in 1999 [sic] and it was also amended later in 1990, just before the elections.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at 65 ter 6128 next, please. Let's look at the decision and see who signed it. 6128 is the number. Page 1. That's page 1. May we turn to the last page to see who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 1st of November, 1991, is the date seen on page 1, and on the last page, was this signed by Kasim Trnka, president of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Dr. Kasim Trnka?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kasim Trnka, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Kasim Trnka was a prominent official of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that he had some connection with that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that he signed this alone as opposed to the decisions taken by the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia, where it was a multi-ethnic group, of multi-ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the decisions that we've seen, this decision compared with those decisions are signed in different manners. I don't know what the practice was in Bosnia as to who would sign those decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina inherited the community of the municipality of Banja Luka as a socio-political entity?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- certainly seems to have replaced it. I'm not sure that the membership was exactly the same; that is, I'm not sure whether all the municipalities that were in the one association community were also in the other. There was a process with the -- the new community of municipalities of individual municipalities actually joining, in other words, sort of rejoining. So it -- it was not simply a change of name or something. It seems to be a new community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 117 of your report you state the following: [In English] "In the early months of 1991, a number of municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, all of which had a Serbian majority or plurality, adopted agreements to form new 'communities of municipalities.' Some of these municipalities simultaneously severing their ties with existing 'communities of municipalities.' Our 'community of municipalities' in the Bosnian Krajina held its founding Assembly session on 25th of April, 1991." [Interpretation] And in paragraph 120 you say: [In English] "The establishment of the ZOBK was perceived by other parties to be an initiative of just one party, SDS. They claimed, moreover, that the primary motivation for the initiative was political rather than economic, the formation of the Serb-dominated regions." [Interpretation] I'd like to underline your conclusion according to which the community of Bosanska Krajina municipalities was together with the Serbs and that the SDS was behind this. What about Kotor Varos, was that part of the Bosanska Krajina municipality?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the membership offhand. I think that some information is given on that in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have 65 ter 4978 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, Mr. Karadzic, I note the time. We'll have a break for 25 minutes now, after which you will have exactly an hour to conclude your cross-examination. We may go to around 2.00, given that the next hearing will start at 2.30. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Donia [sic], do you see here this document where it says that this is an agreement on the association of the municipalities of Bosnian Krajina into a community. The date is 29 April 1991. Do you see the list of municipalities that united together? We can see that on page 1; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is -- those names are on the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say in your conclusion that the association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina were made up of municipalities with a Serb majority and the SDS fully backed this process. Did Kotor Varos municipality join this association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, as it says here? It's on the document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that page of that document doesn't say that those municipalities did, in fact, join the community of municipalities. After this date there was a procedure by which the various municipalities -- the Assemblies of the various municipalities accepted the agreement, that is, adhered to it. Whether Kotor Varos in fact did or not, I cannot recall. It may be in the footnotes to the report as to which particular municipalities we had documentation from that indicated that they actually did adhere to the agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page to see on what basis they formed an association. Article 1: "For the sake of more rational and efficient pursuit of common interests and meeting the needs of the citizens and harmonising socio-economic development of municipalities ..." et cetera, et cetera. It says Kotor Varos joined as well. Can we now see 65 ter 5193.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of Kotor Varos, Dr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Serbs were certainly not an absolute majority; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at page 4 in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that Serbs have 38, Muslims 30, and Croats 29 per cent. Yugoslavs are only 1.9 per cent. Do you agree that Serbs could not make a decision to have Kotor Varos join this association against the will of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what this document is we're looking at. That's certainly what it says, but again, as a general matter, I don't know whether Kotor Varos did or didn't and this -- those figures certainly do indicate that the Serbs were in a relative majority or had a plurality as stated in paragraph 117. I can only speculate about Kotor Varos offhand as I don't know exactly what happened there, but it's entirely possible that some of the non-Serb council members there, members of the Assembly, for one reason or another, agreed to join the new council -- community of municipalities. On the other hand, as we've seen, that there was some -- quite a bit of sharp political manoeuvring going on. It's possible that the Serbian members may have voted on that in the absence of members from other parties. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you should know, Dr. Treanor, that a decision like that cannot be made in the absence of others because such decisions require a majority in parliament. You know how voting is done in our municipalities.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, again we've seen that certain decisions were taken, for instance, in the SRBH Assembly, perhaps in contravention of the rules. But I'm just speculating. I don't know. And I welcome any documentation that you want to bring to my attention and to the Court's attention as to the actual adhesion of Kotor Varos to the community of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at another municipality not so close to the border.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 7 in Serbian and 8 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at Sanski Most, 42 per cent of Serbs, 47 per cent of Muslims, and 7 per cent of Croats. That's 54 per cent of non-Serbs. Do you know that Sanski Most also democratically voted to join the association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I don't know the details of the adhesion of Sanski Most. The -- and the composition of the Municipal Assemblies are not -- are not necessarily exactly reflective of the population breakdown. I don't know offhand the breakdown of party membership in the Assembly of Sanski Most or, as I said, the details of its adhesion to the community. I think there are figures given in the report for how many communities -- municipalities did adhere to the community by a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we come back to 65 ter 4978. This is an agreement signed by these municipalities and we have a list of the municipalities who joined the association -- the community. Kotor Varos and Sanski Most are there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, again, this is the initial agreement. Irrespective of who may have been there at the meeting and signed this particular document, the Assembly of the given municipality would have to ratify the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see D286. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1287, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D286, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The community of municipalities of Banja Luka invites non-Serb municipalities to join." Let us look at the framed part in Serbian. Do you see that the Banja Luka community is inviting municipalities that are majority Muslim and any other municipalities that wish to join their community, to pursue jointly their economic and other interests together? Did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this particular article I can't recall, but that seems to be what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So your conclusion that only Serbs were behind this or that it was intended only for the Serbs does not hold water, does it, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the report says that only Serbian majority or plurality municipalities joined irrespective of who was invited to join, I -- as far as we were able to determine, that -- that it was, in fact, the case that only Serb majority or plurality municipalities did join. The goals and so forth of this community I don't think are very different from the preceding community. So there must have been some reason why it was formed as to replace the old one. But again, the actual membership as opposed to the people that are listed on the putative membership or the -- even people that signed the initial agreement has to be looked at. And insofar as we were able to do that, that's what we found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina were succeeded by the Autonomous Region of Krajina that proclaimed itself in September after Izetbegovic reneged on the Serb-Muslim agreement?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were formed in September, as has been discussed in my testimony and in the report. I don't -- again, referring to the agreement, I don't think there ever was an agreement and I'm not sure at what point Mr. Izetbegovic withdrew from the negotiations in connection with -- in that -- in connection with that agreement together with the SDS and the MBO. I believe that that was in August, so that would put the formation of the Serbian autonomous regions after that particular event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 5405. 5405, just to see the first page of that decision to establish the Autonomous District of Krajina, which was later called "Autonomous Region."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree it says here after the preamble: "Proceeding from the right of every nation to self-determination including secession based on freely expressed will and in keeping with its historic aspirations to live united in the federal state of Yugoslavia as the most suitable form of equal peoples, the Assembly of the community of municipalities proclaims this decision to proclaim the Autonomous Region of Krajina as an inseparable part of the Federal State of Yugoslavia and an integral part of the federal unit of BH." Do you agree that this autonomous region followed from the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina? You deal with it in your paragraph 156.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 138 of the same document you state that the work of other independent regions, autonomous regions -- you say conclusions have to be made because there is no documentation for other autonomous regions. Do you allow the possibility that they were never fully in operation? They remained a dead letter on paper?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your paragraph 141 you state the following: [In English] "In regard to the legal constitutional regime that would apply in the ARK, Article number 3 of the decision on the proclamation of the ARK stated: "'Federal law, regulations, and other general acts, laws regulations and acts of the region, as well as the acts of BH which are not contrary to these acts, shall be applied in the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.'" [Interpretation] And a bit further below: [In English] "'... the laws and regulations and other general acts of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall be applied, unless they are contrary to the Constitution of the SFRY, or to the laws, regulations and other general acts of the Federal State of Yugoslavia.'" We just mentioned it. So the Autonomous Region of Krajina relies on federal regulations and gives precedence to them; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these paragraphs are as you have read them. That, of course, opens the question of who's going to decide whether particular laws are in conformity or are not in conformity. Apparently the autonomous region was going to decide that, which I don't think they were authorised to do under the federal or BH constitutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, in order not to debate it, although I could debate it by saying that Bosnia didn't have the right to secede either, I will just ask you: In your opinion, is it the case that the Autonomous Region of Krajina practically organised itself as a mini state within a state, the government and the Assembly as legislative and executive authorities and autonomy vis-a-v is central organs, precedence to federal laws over republican laws if the latter run counter to the former?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Autonomous Region of Krajina certainly seems to have been pretty well organised, especially in comparison with the other regions for which you lack documentation and maybe that's why we lack documentation, as Dr. Karadzic has pointed out. However, Dr. Karadzic was very insistent that the deputies and officials of the organs in the Autonomous Region of Krajina who were members of the SDS or followers of the SDS follow SDS policy. He didn't really make any distinction between whether someone was in a -- holding a party position or a government position as an SDS appointee or electee. So that he certainly attempted to keep the Autonomous Region of Krajina under control. There were some difficulties in that regard. I think we mentioned some of them, but that certainly was his desire and effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the case that the officials of the Autonomous Region of Krajina were elected in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, nobody else elected them?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were elected by the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which was composed of delegated members from the municipal -- from the Assemblies of the municipalities that were members of the region, the vast majority of which I think would have been members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in paragraph 151 you note what the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina regulated and what it left to the autonomous regions to deal with. So would you focus on that paragraph of yours. Do you agree that the constitution gives a lot of leeway for the municipalities to see to their own affairs? In other words, there's no regulation or the central organs do not prescribe conduct. So the regions have a lot of leeway in organising life as they see fit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the regions run the discussion here, yes. The areas of responsibility are laid out here; however, the regions were not established under the constitution as very powerful entities. There was a controversy about that. Previous -- or drafts of the constitution had included references to the -- or provision that the autonomous regions have governments and other organs aside from the Assembly that the final constitution as adopted only gave the autonomous regions Assemblies, and this was regarded with some dissatisfaction certainly in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which did have a government. And that was one of the issues that led to the problems in Banja Luka at the end of February 1992 that we may have discussed previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember, and paragraphs 158 -- or rather, and 161 speak about that, that the Assembly of Republika Srpska in September 1992 decided to start centralisation of the government and to try and reduce the authority that the regions had so as to exercise greater control. Is that what you say there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 158?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. And 161. [In English] "Several documents of subsequent" --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those paragraphs deal with that issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the central Assembly considered that what the regions had was too much and needed to be centralised in September 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and there were also comments in the Assembly made to the effect that the regions had served their purpose, which was to help dismantle Izetbegovic's state or Alija's state, I think, as they referred to it, so they were no longer needed. And what was needed now was a centralisation in the Bosnian Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at D283.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you tender 5405?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Momir, and I think that was Momir Jungic, who was the head of the cultural and educational community.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the date is the 8th of June, 1991. And Karadzic says: "We have to prepare the laws -- the legal regulations in order that the regions have their money at their disposal and to ... the republic, to send for the republic needs a certain portion. And not to centralise everything and then ..." "No, they will give to the republic, but they ... not that I get back 18 dinars out of 100 dinars ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we turn to page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "It would be a good idea to speed up the process so that the region could feel that they can dispose of their money as they see fit and develop cultural life ..." And then lower down: "At the level of the municipality -- everything at the level of the municipality, libraries and so on, at the level of the region, that which is the region's, the theatre and things like that ..." And then: "That they should have full dominion over their resources. "And that they send to the republic, well, that is democracy, there is no more redistribution in the socialist fashion, when you collect everything and then you give as much as you want."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "They have been deprived in that way -- they have been robbed in that respect." Now, are you aware of the socialist system, whereby all the monies flew in -- were pooled into a central piggy bank and then distributed locally?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how much the municipalities were -- for instance, were able to retain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, they weren't allowed to retain anything, Dr. Treanor. They had to hand in everything and then wait for the republic to hand out as much as it wanted, and that's what they wanted to change, not to have to wait for the republic to send them resources. So this is the redistribution that is mentioned here. And do you know that Banja Luka slipped down to 18th place in development terms? It was the 18th-most developed town, whereas it used to be the second-most developed -- most highly developed town?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know its place in the development ranks, but as I mentioned in the course of my testimony earlier, there was a great deal of grass-roots support for regionalisation. And we're seeing here one of the reasons why, that is, that money was getting sent to the capital and it wasn't coming back, so that people wanted to keep control over more of their own resources. That was certainly one of the grass-roots incentives for the formation of regions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 65 ter 30048 next, please. 30048. It's a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Radoslav Brdjanin and Mice Cvjetkovic on the 19th of June, 1991. They didn't even let me celebrate my birthday properly. May we turn to page 8 in the English and page 5 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am talking to them here and towards the bottom of the page: "You can link up everything, economic and everything else ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page in the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "You can link up everything but not in the state respect. I don't want any linkage in state terms." And Brdjanin asks: "Territorially we can't mention everything." And Karadzic says: "No, at -- certainly not ..." And then he goes on to say that: "We should stay with the functional and economic ..." Did you know about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall this specific conversation. It's quite likely that I did read it, though. What's being referenced here, as I think we have discussed before, is the effort to unite Bosnian Krajina with Croatian Krajina at the end of June 1991, something that Dr. Karadzic and the SDS leaders in Sarajevo were opposed to in view of negotiations that were going on at that time with Muslim leaders in Bosnia, if for no other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 1289, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 65 ter 30123 next, please. This is a telephone conversation held in July between Karadzic and Brdjanin. May we turn to page 4 of the Serbian and 7 of the English. K says, Karadzic: "We want the whole of Bosnia, the whole of Bosnia is our fatherland. I mean, we want -- we have the right to it and no one has the right to take us out of Yugoslavia. Regardless of whether we're in the minority or the majority. Regardless of what percentage it is and we will regionalise Bosnia and allow them to make a region. They can have Cazin. They can make a region. Not a problem."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in July our position was that Bosnia should remain whole, an entity, and be regionalised within?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the position that was put forward in the document that we saw earlier what the Serbs propose, which was based on an earlier document passed by the SDS club of deputies in the SRBH Assembly. I would just note that these conversations with Mr. Brdjanin are with someone who was a prominent SDS official, indeed a deputy in the SRBH Assembly, and that the heads of all the other organs in the Autonomous Region of Krajina were occupied by -- also occupied by SDS people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document and then we can move on to the next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will mark it for identification as D1290.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have 65 ter 30056, please -- 30256, which is the conversation between Karadzic and the late Predrag Radic, who was the mayor of Banja Luka, on the 20th of September, 1991. 3026 is the document number -- 30256. Page 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Predrag Radic says at the top: "Last night on television it was announced that this man Naim said that there would be an SDP and SDA gathering here and I think the subject is regionalisation. Now, if they are going -- if they are going to be the only ones to talk about reorganisation and not us, then I don't think that's all right." And lower down Karadzic says: "We weren't invited. They prepared the draft of a statement which their intellectuals are going to sign." And then a little further down, Karadzic says: "... however, we have negotiations at 10.00 again with Izetbegovic and it's all in keeping with our negotiations. The only thing is that we are moving a little faster than we agreed, but they are also being petty and hypocrites. They are discussing one thing with Silajdzic advocating and something quite different."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we turn to page 3 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Karadzic says to Radic: "You have to be masters of your own goods ..." And then a little lower down: "There is no power without that." And then: "The Muslims will accept all this because we're not going to do anything by force or without having reached a prior agreement." And then he goes on to say: "What they do in Zenica we shall do in Banja Luka." And lower down: "Sarajevo has special status, that's another matter, but there's no doubt that we are doing this in accordance with our agreements. The fact that they are having trouble getting used to it is another matter." Do you know that everything we did was agreed upon with Izetbegovic, whereas we implemented the agreement straight away and it was their intention to deceive us?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any agreement. I know the discussions which were going on about this time for the so-called historic agreement included regionalisation, but that agreement never came to fruition. And I don't know what the reference is to the meeting that the people are holding and what the tenor of that meeting might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not forbid anything but just made recommendations that the formation of new regions be stopped?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct. And they also passed a resolution against the unification of Bosnian Krajina with Croatian Krajina at the end of June 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, MFI D1291. Mr. Karadzic, you have 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have 1D3564.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know how the other two sides behaved in Bosnia in this respect? Do you know what the Croatian side did?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the HDZ -- some of its leaders were engaged in the summer and fall of 1991 in establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document testifies to that and the 6th of Kolovoz, as they say, is the 6th of August. And we have "Kolovoz" here translated as "August" here, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have Serbian page 6, or rather, Croatian page 6 and English page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the entire document is devoted to what you just talked about, creation of Croatian regions. Look at paragraph 21: "The proposal of the regional HDZ union from Travnik to found regional unions in order to establish the closest possible links between Croatian people, is passed. On the basis of such links it is necessary to make detailed proposals, feasibility studies, regarding the justifiability of the regional territory linking the Croatian people ..." So is this a parallel process then within the Yugoslav crisis and Bosnian crisis, for the Croatian people to organise themselves along those lines?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, broadly parallel. It's also parallel to the process that took place in Croatia among the Croatian Serbs, that is, the formation of communities of municipalities, the formation of a Serbian National Council, and the formation of Serbian autonomous regions, and the final declaration of a republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 24 of your report, P92, where you speak about the position of Karadzic as president of the party. [In English] "In short, the Presidency was the single-most important central party institution ..." [Interpretation] And then paragraph 25: [In English] "... a frequent and repeated message from Karadzic to SDS leaders in the field was insistence on the respect of the party hierarchy and discipline. Karadzic was able to communicate easily in this way with municipal SDS leaders, too, as and when the situation required and to co-ordinate party work at various levels." [Interpretation] Paragraph 26 also says that: "Karadzic, within the frameworks of his party, acted with impunity." [In English] "In fact, within the party per se, Karadzic acted with virtual impunity." [Interpretation] So in your report you portray me as an autocrat and as somebody who is absolute and nobody can do anything to. Right? Paragraph 41 is similar, as is 67. These paragraphs indicate the kind of person I was and my position in the party. Whether it relates to the founding of the SDS as a central party, where strict discipline is adhered to, that in the SDS Karadzic is particularly powerful and his closest associates who lead the party, that Karadzic should be considered an autocrat, dictator, and the embodiment of all things non-democratic. That's what you say; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does paragraph 67 say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your paragraphs suggest that my position in the party is the position of an autocrat, that of an autocrat and somebody who can do anything without being punished.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we have 65 ter 30048 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You just made a statement without asking a question or without hearing from the witness. Do you wish to answer the question, Mr. -- Dr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think there was a question there somewhere. Right. Well, the report does not use the word "autocrat." I don't want to get bogged down on semantic points, but it certainly portrays Mr. Karadzic as being a very strong party leader, strong and active.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have 65 ter 30048 next, please. We have very little time left, but I just want us to see how Karadzic -- what Karadzic's attitude was towards democracy, quasi democracy, and discipline. Page 6 in English. The document is 30048, 65 ter 30048 is what we need. Page 4 in Serbian and 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is what we already looked at, MFI D1289.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you see that longest sentence -- that longest paragraph where he says: "Those idiots are working to Tudjman's advantage ..." And then towards the bottom he says: "I cannot understand why I allowed so much lack of discipline in the party and so much false or quasi democracy in the party ..." Now, Dr. Treanor, do you know that the SDS cadres and membership criticised me for doing quite the reverse, that I gave too much leeway to democracy and non-discipline in the party, and we had a witness here yesterday who testified to that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have 30357, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, in those intercepts did you happen to note all the oral struggles I had with people, first and foremost in Banja Luka, for them to respect what had been agreed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here is one such conversation held on the 16th of October, 1991, the day after the adoption of that declaration on independence. And when we stepped down from -- upon leaving the Assembly I talked to Dr. Vukic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have page 5 in Serbian and 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: Karadzic: "When this political struggle is over, when it's all over, when the state is saved, I will sign the undertaking now that I will leave politics. Of course they will leave too. Nobody will elect such fools again. But let the people elect whom they want, but let them not try to occupy offices now in a state that does not exist ..." Do you know that I had to fight not only for the making of decisions and finding solutions, but to have these decisions implemented and I met with a lot of resistance and trouble?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are many conversations where Dr. Karadzic tries to get people to do things that have already been decided or not to go against what had already been decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly look at P1084.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a telephone conversation in July between Karadzic and Vojo Kupresanin, who was president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. At that moment it was just a community of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Karadzic: "I'm asking you nicely. The meeting of the Main Board is on Thursday. On Thursday we'll clear up things once and for all, whether these people belong to the party that is implementing this policy or is it another party. We have to clear that up. I cannot engage in politics when people there are doing things without authorisation. That's an unauthorised move. It cannot be done without the Main Board ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Karadzic says: "Well, the Serbian Democratic Party -- it's harder -- I have a harder time with our own people than with our adversaries ..." And the last line: "Of course it's harder to deal with our own people ..." Does this reflect my efforts that democratic decisions be honoured?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it only reflects the difficulties that were had in trying to get decisions honoured, as you put it. I don't know what you mean by "democratic decisions." The reference here seems to be to the Main Board which may have made a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's now time for you to conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another five minutes as you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, just conclude in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at D282 -- D280. Your Excellencies, the entire segment about the interviews with Mr. Cizmovic remains outstanding, although Dr. Treanor assigned in his report various roles to Mr. Cizmovic that he didn't have. That's my problem. This is a conversation between Karadzic and Kupresanin. We need page 6 in both versions. It says "Radovan" halfway down. "The Serbian Assembly made a decision Saturday and Sunday, 7.00 to 7.00 p.m. Nobody can change it, neither Karadzic nor Milosevic, nor God himself. From 7.00 to 1900 hours, that's what the Assembly decided! "If the Assembly decided, who am I to change it? I am just a small player who is serving that Assembly and the entire party and the entire Serbian people! I am neither a big shot or a big boss to change things and neither is he, Vukic! Nobody among us! We are here to serve the Assembly."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't it clear that the Main Board is the main body in the party and the Assembly for the state?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Assembly assigned itself a certain role. The Assembly, of course, was composed almost entirely of members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look again at P12 and that will be the end. Unfortunately, I kindly ask that it be taken into account that the OTP interviews with Mr. Cizmovic are in complete contrast with the conclusions made in this report and that it be taken into account. Can we look towards the bottom of page 1, English page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We -- that's my speech at the extended session of the Main Board on the 14th of February, the day after the beginning of official negotiations. "We hope that deputies will intensify their activities in municipalities because deputy is power, parties are a service elected by people, a service to the people to have the popular will exercised. Parties are not our government, they are not our main authority. Authority belongs to the Assembly and deputies."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then page 15 Serbian, English page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "500.000 Serbs, million Serbs outside Krajina, and we have to agree. If this policy is wrong, then the Main Board has to say so today that it leads to a dead end, that not a single objective has been achieved so far, and then we should change the leadership. I will personally be grateful to you. You will give me a medal or a member -- or an honourable member because I was the first president of the party and I will be happy to move into a different sort of politics, to move with a different policy. If there is a different policy and I'm not implementing it, we deserve to be replaced." And then it says: "The greatest authority in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is the Serbian Assembly and don't mess around with it."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 16, English page 22, last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conclude as soon as possible. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "I don't want to be at the head of this party for a day longer. I believe I have done my -- I have repaid my debt to the people. I can't wait to go back to my profession. Of course you will find a replacement. Nobody is irreplaceable." Did you know that the party and myself within that party were handing over power to the elected people in various authorities and we had no desire to exercise power ourselves?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's one of the things that is said in the report, that the SDS sort of melded in with the Bosnian Serb governmental structures that were established, all of whom -- all of which structures were staffed by people from the -- from the SDS. I note the reference here to apparently giving the Main Board the final word in a particular position here. Again, the Bosnian Serb Assembly and the Municipal Assemblies being referenced were composed of SDS people, and Dr. Karadzic was always insistent that they carry out party policy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Treanor, I'll obviously be brief under the circumstances. First I'd like to bring you back to something the accused raised yesterday, and that was a speech by Dr. Kalinic at the 4th Assembly Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina on 21 December cited in support of -- of a proposition that the Serbs recognised that all three peoples had the right to sovereign control of their lives in territories where they were the majority. Could I refer you quickly to another passage of that same Assembly where the accused said, and that's at page 38 of that Assembly: "We have the right and the ability to prevent anybody on the territories where we conducted our referendum to secede from Yugoslavia in all territories where Serbs took part in the referendum. Regardless of whether they make 5 per cent or 55 per cent of the population, they are the constituent element of that town or that republic. All territories where we voted in our referendum to remain within Yugoslavia must stay within Yugoslavia if we decide so." Does that statement by Dr. Karadzic reflect on the territories and areas over which the Bosnian Serb leaders considered Serbs should be sovereign?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I remember that passage because the 5 per cent figure struck me. That would make the potential Serbian area within Bosnia and Herzegovina quite extensive. Dr. Karadzic frequently made reference to the fact that Serbs owned 64 per cent of the land in Bosnia, something which was not technically true. But that statement along with this one would seem to indicate a very extensive claim to -- on the part of the Bosnian Serbs to land in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Today, earlier, the accused put to you that what was termed or what I think you termed "the Sarajevo Agreement" left only maps to be decided. Now, I want to set aside for a -- your -- for purposes of this question your response, that the document was -- only served as a basis for further negotiations but just concentrate for a moment on the maps. And in that connection I wanted to turn your attention to D20 at -- which is the shorthand record from the 11th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held on the 18th of March, 1992, the same date as the Sarajevo Agreement. And turn to a portion where the accused explained to the Assembly deputies the following concerning the negotiations. "What we have here is a process," he said, "and the mistake that Dobrivoje is making has to do with the fact that an unfinished process should not be assessed as if it were a finished one. We have entered into this process with our strategic goals and we are accomplishing them stage by stage ..." And then he continued: "We have preserved the Serbian people as a corpus in its entirety in the BH and attached it as an entity and now it is a matter of quantity only. We have achieved the quality. This is what Europe recognises. Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina exists. The only remaining question is the one of quantity and it will happen according our political will, our right to self-determination and organisation. It will happen according to the conditions which are up to you to create." Was -- can you explain in the context you have just been describing, very quickly, the -- how this affected the issues concerning the maps and their completion at this time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned, the map was simply a map showing the relative majorities, ethnic majorities, in the municipalities. It was by no means designed to be a final map of the constituent units, and Dr. Karadzic is here indicating how the final boundaries of the Serbian unit might be created, referring to -- being a step in a process -- steps in a process. As I indicated, the strategy at this time -- the Bosnian Serb strategy was to create their own entity, assert control over those territories within a confederation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a view to eventually attaching those territories to a broader Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you said it is P20 on 11th -- it should be P12. Is it not P12?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I was -- sorry, Your Honour. I was referring to the 11th Session of the Assembly, which I understood to be D00020.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you check it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure, I'm sorry. That's -- sorry. It's D0090. With the -- if -- I don't know if the Court wants to view that document, otherwise I will be moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Treanor, you referred yesterday to the consistent position of the Bosnian Serb leadership concerning their intention to -- over the long term to unite with Serbia and other Serbian entities, thereby splitting up Bosnia. And you also referred to the fact that that intention was not emphasised by the Bosnian Serbs during the course of the negotiations. Can I turn your attention to 65 ter 06139, please, page 19 of both the English and the B/C/S. This is a session of the SFRY Presidency held on March 2nd, 1991. And this -- there Dr. Karadzic says -- it refers to how they're constantly -- "the European community, especially the United States, is constantly warning that BiH is not to be split up and we accepted it. We will not split up. This is not about splitting up but about an internal transformation and they swallowed the bait. Europe swallowed the bait." And I wanted to ask you whether this is a reflection of some of the terminology used in the course of the negotiations and the emphasis or non-emphasis placed on the ultimate goal of unification?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes the negotiations --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This calls for speculation. The first question was leading and this one calls for speculation. And I don't have a chance to test it later or to challenge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've heard the repeated use of the term "transformation," and it is now being placed in context and the witness is being asked to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, as an expert he can comment on it as far as he can. Yes, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the negotiations were all about the transformation of BH. The idea of uniting portions of BH with -- or the desire to unite portions of BH with any other state were not -- was not voiced in the framework of those negotiations, rather the contrary. But as I think we've seen today in some of the things we've seen but certainly in other sessions of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, that that was still the desire of the Bosnian Serbs and their leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I would tender this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2587, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Treanor, today at page 27, at least of today's transcript, the accused referred you to an intercept with Gojko Djogo of 12 October 1992 and directed your attention to, as he had in -- with a number of previous intercepts, to what he called "preparing for war." Now, let me focus on that Djogo-Karadzic conversation on 12 October 1991, where Dr. Karadzic says at page 2: "We led them but they are preparing for war. They will try to wage war here." Djogo says: "They will." Karadzic says: "Probably as soon as next week." And then Djogo says: "Where -- where is he going to war?" Karadzic says: "Well, he's crazy. They're -- they're totally crazy you know ..." et cetera. I wanted you to place this in context for us, Dr. Treanor. What threat was paramount in the minds of the Bosnian Serbs as far as the documentary record reflects at this point in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this point the Bosnian -- the Assembly of SRBiH had begun a joint session and this was the session at which the resolutions on the sovereignty of BH were introduced and were under discussion. So I think that was the threat that was uppermost in the minds of Bosnian Serb leaders at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that referenced in further portions of the intercept, for example, at page 7, where Dr. Karadzic says: "No, they have inflamed irresponsible deputies with the notion that they should get a state?" Or at page 9 of the intercept, Dr. Karadzic says: "We will not force them to do anything but they simply don't have any way to carry out a secession"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's reflective of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the time of this intercept did you see any reflections in the documentary record that the Bosnian Serb leadership was concerned about an -- or did you see any threats by the Bosnian Muslim leadership of an imminent military aggression against the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In fact, if I could go back to the A and B document that we discussed, in the preamble of that document it lays out the reason for its existence which it describes as a possible forcible attempt to take BH out of Yugoslavia as in the Bosnian Serb leadership's conception. "Forcible" would mean the type of action that was taken on October 15th in -- in voting the sovereignty resolutions which Dr. Karadzic described as constitutional violence. That document makes no reference to any imminent threat. I was asked whether it was defensive. It is defensive in the sense that the whole Bosnian Serb project at that time was defensive, that is, to defend the rights of the Bosnian Serb people to remain in Yugoslavia, which involves efforts to define and assert control over territory. It is not defensive in the sense that they expected some sort of imminent military threat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we have to leave -- rise. Is it okay? Would it be okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It will have to be, Your Honour. Let me just note two things quickly as we rise. Number one, our bar table submission, which is very succinct, is still pending and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is joined by the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean the recently filed -- I mean in connection with -- appendix B to this -- to the 92 ter submission. And we tried to be as judicious as possible under the circumstances, in light of the truncated period for the re-direct, I'll consider if any additions are necessary, but I understand the Court's position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And theoretically the Prosecution's motion of the 6th of June, confidential motion to resume the testimony of Mr. -- Dr. Treanor, but given that his evidence is completed, I take it that has been disposed of?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we can reclassify it as public?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, just one question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we have to rise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One short question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is quite unfair. I didn't get to complete my re-direct, and -- and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will rise, Dr. Karadzic. That concludes your evidence, Dr. Treanor. I thank you, and have a safe trip back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I hope I was able to assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.00 p.m.,
